sections.html:
Chelsea is a Suffolk County city on a small peninsula in Boston Harbor, tied to Boston by the Tobin Bridge. At about 2.2 square miles of land it is the smallest city in Massachusetts, yet the 2020 census counted 40,787 people, and 14,554 housing units, 5.2 percent of them vacant. That makes for dense blocks of wood-frame multifamily buildings.

Two big fires, one in 1908 and one in 1973, shaped much of what stands today. The city came back from 1908 with wider streets, while 1973 tore through tightly packed multifamily buildings. Fire safety remains part of every sale here, since a smoke and carbon monoxide certificate has to be in hand before the deed passes.

Chelsea has several named areas, each with its own housing mix.

  • Admirals Hill holds the Naval Hospital Historic District and Mary O'Malley Park, the city's largest park.
  • Addison-Orange is flat, residential and densely populated.
  • Bellingham Square is the center of commerce and government, with City Hall and the public library.
  • The Box District, named for early box factories, was rezoned for residential use in the 2000s.
  • Carter Park and Wyndham are a small enclave of mostly single-family Queen Anne homes.
  • Mill Hill has mostly two- and three-story wood-frame detached buildings.
  • Prattville is the northwestern section, and Soldiers Home covers Powderhorn Hill.

Tell buyers which area you are in. A single-family house in Carter Park draws a different buyer than a three-decker in Mill Hill.

sections.h2: Rates, exemptions and the assessor's office
sections.html:
Chelsea's Assessing Department values every property in the city and handles residential and statutory exemptions. The residential exemption is worth $3,203.68 in tax dollars, equal to $279,066 in assessed value. Ask the assessors whether your home qualifies.

The office is in Room 211 at City Hall, 500 Broadway, and the phone is 617-466-4010. Hours are Monday to Thursday, 8 a.m. to 4 p.m., Tuesday evening from 4 to 7 p.m., and Friday morning until noon. The Assessor page has forms and the property record cards.

The MBTA Silver Line SL3 runs from South Station to four Chelsea stops: Eastern Avenue, Box District, Downtown Chelsea and Mystic Mall. It also connects to Logan Airport and to the Blue Line at Airport Station. A commuter rail station on the Newburyport/Rockport Line serves North Station, and several bus routes reach East Boston, Revere and Everett.

Route 1 is a limited-access highway that cuts the city in half, and the Tobin Bridge carries it to Charlestown. Transit access is a real selling point here, so mention how close the house is to a Silver Line or rail stop.

sections.h2: What should a Chelsea seller prepare before closing?
sections.html:
The deed excise tax is $2.00 for each $500 of price or fraction of $500 under MGL c. 64D, s. 1. The county registry of deeds collects it at recording, and the Assessor page links to the Suffolk County Registry of Deeds.

  • Schedule the smoke and carbon monoxide inspection with the Chelsea Fire Department once you have a closing date.
  • Pull the deed, tax bill and any permit records.
  • If tenants live there, gather leases and note rents.
  • If the house is inherited, ask the probate court or an attorney what is needed first.

Many Chelsea sellers own a two- or three-family. Before you list, collect each lease, note the rent and the end date, and confirm any permits for work done on the units. Buyers and lenders look at those records first. If the unit is occupied, showings need tenant cooperation, and that can stretch the timeline.

Wood-frame buildings packed close together also draw careful inspections of wiring, heating and egress. Fixing known issues before an inspector finds them can protect your price, though some owners prefer to sell as is and let the buyer take on the work.

Chelsea is bordered by water on three sides: the Island End River toward Everett, the Mystic River and Chelsea Creek toward Boston, and Mill Creek along part of the Revere line. Most of the waterfront from the Tobin Bridge to the mouth of Mill Creek is a designated port area and stays largely industrial. For a seller, that means a house near the water may sit beside working industrial land, so be ready to describe the block honestly.

Hills such as Admirals Hill, Mount Bellingham, Powderhorn Hill, Mount Washington and Mill Hill break the flat ground into distinct pockets, which is part of why neighborhood names matter so much when you describe a property.

A seller who starts the folder early saves time later. Put in the deed, the current tax bill, permit records, any lease and rent record for each unit, and notes on repairs made over the years. Keep the assessor's property record card too, since buyers sometimes ask what the city has on file for the building.

If the house came to you through an estate, ask the probate court or an attorney what has to be done before a deed can be signed. That step can set the earliest possible closing date, so it is better to learn about it at the start than at the end.

Once you accept an offer, the usual order is a purchase agreement, inspections, the fire department certificate, and then closing. The deed is signed and recorded, the excise tax is paid, and any tax balance comes out of the proceeds. Your closing attorney can confirm what is owed. If you inherited the house, the probate step comes first, so start there.

For an owner who wants to skip showings and repairs, Cash Home Buyers can look at a Chelsea house as it stands and give you a written offer to compare with a listing. Compare it with an agent's estimate after subtracting repair costs, fees and the months a listing can take.

It tends to suit owners with an inherited house, tenants who complicate showings, a building that needs heavy repair, or a move that cannot wait. If the house is in good shape and you have time, a regular listing may bring more. Either way, ask for terms in writing before you commit.

faqs.q: What county is Chelsea, MA in?
faqs.a: Suffolk County, the same county as Boston. It sits across the Mystic River from Charlestown.

faqs.q: Is Chelsea the smallest city in Massachusetts?
faqs.a: Yes. At about 2.2 square miles of land, it is the smallest city in the state by land area.

faqs.q: What was the Great Chelsea Fire?
faqs.a: On April 12, 1908, a fire destroyed nearly half the city and left 18,000 people homeless. A second fire in 1973 destroyed 18 city blocks.

faqs.q: What is Chelsea's residential tax rate?
faqs.a: The fiscal year 2026 residential rate is $11.48 per $1,000 of assessed value. The commercial, industrial and personal property rate is $23.79.

faqs.q: Do I need a smoke and CO certificate to sell in Chelsea?
faqs.a: Yes. The state requires a compliance certificate from the local fire department for any home sale or transfer.
